### 2026-10-03 — This is the project I have been working on for a long time now. It is an ESP32-based inventory manager and dashboard. Its primary purpose is to help me keep timers for studying, Pomodoro, and other ac

**4.7h**

This is the project I have been working on for a long time now. It is an ESP32-based inventory manager and dashboard. Its primary purpose is to help me keep timers for studying, Pomodoro, and other activities. In addition, it tells me the location of almost 230 modules I own.

![IMG_20260930_161512](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/650c5c4382daee9d6746028784166092bba1bce4c0eaa426635156d4dff0e2db.jpg)

![IMG_20260927_155842](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/7222e5f6849d9b48b04015c20736288fb1fc3e4612f529188857e1a8c95ec2ba.jpg)

Looking into the details, I have an ESP32 as the main microcontroller, and I use most of its functionalities except Bluetooth. Next, we have the SSD1306 OLED module. I am looking to update it to a TFT display because the current OLED display is relatively small and difficult to see while sitting at my bench. The OLED display is followed by a small button, a toggle switch that I can use to turn it on and off, and an RTC module to track the time correctly because I will not be keeping the device turned on continuously, as I only have a 2,200 mAh battery in it.

Next, we have the most important part, of course: the keypad module. This is a 4-by-4 keypad module in which I have introduced a Nokia-style button keypad. Pressing a single button multiple times triggers a letter. For example, pressing button 5 twice gives the letter K.

During this specific session, I integrated the RTC module because, in the previous version, the RTC module was not working at all. It was not even being detected. I diagnosed the problem as the SDA and SCL lines being switched. I was also sharing those SDA and SCL lines with my OLED module. I changed that from pin 2 to pins 16 and 17, and used the SDA and SCL lines for the RTC module.

![17910094699313928562183987608223](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/d0f93282bba0a94ae72e19c8b3d97763289ffd92581db19bc1daa611b356dbba.jpg)

Integrating this RTC module was quite a bit of work because I had never interfaced any of my microcontrollers with an RTC module before. I first wrote a test sketch and was able to retrieve almost all the details, but the time was offset. I bought a new coin cell for it because the old one was nearly dead. In the sketch I wrote, I updated the time to the correct date and hour.

![Screenshot_20261003-121354](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/ff7e4210de97bcde8a7456d0251fb31a7e39ce167923f168f5d9ac9d3561fcd2.png)

The next thing I did during this session was secure the connections so that the previous issue of the keypad module disconnecting automatically would be resolved. In addition, I made many software changes. The ESP32 was consuming a lot of power because the OLED module was turned on at all times, and it was calculating time in three to four layers simultaneously. To reduce that, I implemented light sleep, which is a step below deep sleep. In light sleep, only the OLED module stays active, and if a clock is needed, the RTC module is also used. However, the anti-semodule consumes very little power, which is negligible. By using this and reducing the loop cycle, I was successfully able to reduce the current consumption and thereby increase the lifespan of the device.

![Screenshot_20261003-121342](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/78e3bc7ec725093219a9ccbfba8985a5483958cb52b0778b62ff1d2246785941.png)

In the next session, I am looking forward to adding an INMP441 microphone module so that I can talk to this module like an agent and trigger it by calling its name, such as, “Hey, Jarvis.” It will then turn on, and I will be able to command it by saying, “Hey, Jarvis, go to the inventory. I also want to take an OLED module with an ESP32-CAM "   the agent inside my ESP32 will update the LittleFS storage, allowing me to do that hands-free.(The blank space below the oled is reserved for future modules,including inmp441  ,vibration motor,etc)
